# Lessons index: Building with AI (generated, do not edit)

One SHORTENED line per lesson: the condition and the instruction, routinely dropping the
clause saying what the failure looks like. Read the whole entry before a rule decides
anything: `~/claude-config-sync/claude-sync lesson L174`, or the entry in ~/.claude/LESSONS.md,
which is NOT loaded into the session.

- L860. A review that says safe means merge and file its optional items as issues; a build round for them brings another review that finds more.
- L861. A review suggestion proposing a new guard, scanner or library is a new piece with its own issue, never a fix round of the piece reviewed.
- L862. State whether a source reading guard stops honest mistakes or deliberate hiding, and tell every reviewer, or each round hunts a new disguise.
- L863. One blocking bar for every review round of a piece; after round two an item blocks only if today's code or a named planned change reaches it.
- L832. Put a prompt cache point where shared text ends, and confirm real traffic rereads it within its lifetime: a write nobody reads costs extra.
- L828. A thinking model's output cap covers its thinking: size it for both, and refuse any reply that stopped at the cap.
- L820. An AI call handling dates must be given today's date and time zone in its context; without it a guessed date passes every format check.
- L816. A streamed model reply ending in an error or with no finish must fail the call; the SDK still returns the partial text as if whole.
- L814. Record fixed consent text as shown only on the page's confirmed render, and fill its blanks from sources no model or chat input can write.
- L1029. Put a prompt's fixed text first and the per call parts after: the cache reuses only an unchanged opening, so one early varying line re-bills it all.
- L768. An AI check reading a large artifact once is a sample, so recheck loops never converge: verify references by script and split the rest.
- L270. A rule stated in a prompt is contradicted by every example that breaks it, and the demonstration outweighs the instruction.
- L27. A rule that lives only in a prompt is a hope.
- L194. A payload reducing a stored fact to a FLAG ABOUT ITSELF tells its reader the fact exists while denying it the value, and the rediscovery can fail.
- L28. Treat a detached AI run as an untrusted subprocess.
- L128. A field whose only writer is an AI prompt, and whose ABSENCE is a legitimate value, cannot tell an ignored instruction from a considered judgement.
- L161. When an AI writes a fact the system already HOLDS, check what it wrote AGAINST that value: a presence check passes a contradicted fact.
- L328. A reader that can INDEPENDENTLY source what the payload failed to send succeeds for a reason the sender never supplied, hiding the omission.
- L333. Agents dispatched on ONE brief each reach the same finding, so any outward action they can take alone arrives as N records of one defect.
- L167. An AI writer that can READ the consuming code derives its contract from that code's permissiveness, so an optional field is permission, not neutrality.
- L249. A decision ATTRIBUTED to somebody inside your own artifact must be quoted from the record that holds it and carry that record's own date.
- L340. A defensive normalization that coerces a response into the shape you asked for destroys the only evidence the instruction was ignored.
- L363. A deduplication running before findings are filed must compare against the store they are filed INTO, or any audit of it restates its own records.
- L660. A claim that a shared mechanism already covers your code is checkable in one command, so check it rather than asserting it
